campaign.title: Derive and exploit the one-sided top-block transform

conductor_policy.monitoring: Check endpoint half-weight conventions, the odd-h quarter-integer separation, boundary stationary transitions, actual beta coefficients, and the exact implication to the top M2 block.
conductor_policy.round_close: Close only after an exact one-sided transform or a rigorous obstruction is proved and independently scoped.

numerical_purpose: falsify an endpoint constant or parity-separation claim
resource_policy.numerical_prohibition: Finite transforms cannot certify a uniform asymptotic estimate.
resource_policy.literature_policy: Use primary sources for discontinuous Poisson or endpoint stationary phase only if a non-elementary theorem is imported.

frozen_target.sum: For y=floor(sqrt X), w_end(d)=W(d/y)1_(d<=y), and odd h<=H_y=floor(yX^(-1/4)), transform or directly bound sum_(d<=y) w_end(d)e(hX/(4d)) with all endpoint terms explicit.
frozen_target.key_separation: Prove or refute that dist(hX/(4y^2),Z)>=c for every surviving odd h<=H_y and large X, preventing a stationary point from coalescing with u=1.
frozen_target.success: Either prove the top M2 frequency block is O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)) uniformly in 1<=L<=X^(1/4), or reduce it to an exact strictly cleaner signed cone/packet estimate with a target-sized boundary term.

exit_gates: exact endpoint Poisson convention and half-weight
stationary and nonstationary errors summed over h
actual signed cone or direct top-block estimate
campaign.promotion_policy: Promote only an exact endpoint transform, a proved target-sized boundary contribution, a scoped top-block range, or a rigorous obstruction. Do not infer the smooth small-gcd packet estimate from endpoint algebra.
